topic: Why did dinosaurs grow to be so big?
topic_context: Potential explanations include access to food sources, temperature regulation, protection from predators, and other factors.
scientific_reframing: Which interacting anatomical, life-history, physiological, and ecological conditions enabled repeated evolution of extreme body mass in sauropods, and which conditions are necessary, sufficient, or only correlated with gigantism?

selected_primary_direction.name: GigaCascade
selected_primary_direction.title: Fossil-Anchored Causal Comparison of Constraint Release in Sauropod Gigantism
selected_primary_direction.central_hypothesis: Extreme sauropod body mass became evolutionarily accessible when feeding architecture, axial pneumaticity, growth/life-history capacity, and ecological opportunity jointly crossed lineage-specific feasibility thresholds; the interaction model must predict held-out giant lineages better than single-factor or additive alternatives.
candidate_blocks: feeding architecture: neck/body geometry, head and dental-processing proxies
pneumatic anatomy: axial skeletal pneumaticity and anatomical confidence
growth/life history: histological and ontogenetic proxies
ecological opportunity: facies, paleoflora, geography, and sampling context
falsification_conditions: No leave-clade-out predictive advantage over preregistered simple alternatives.
Candidate enabling traits systematically appear after mass transitions.
Model ranking reverses under plausible mass, phylogeny, or trait-coding uncertainty.
A small number of taxa or formations dominate the apparent signal.
selected_primary_direction.claim_ceiling: Conditional support for a macroevolutionary feasibility model; not a direct measurement of extinct metabolism, ventilation, thermoregulation, daily intake, or behavior.

research_conclusion: The strongest evidence-based explanation is multi-constraint rather than monogenic or single-factor: repeated sauropod giant size may reflect an interaction among efficient access to forage, body-plan and pneumatic-anatomy constraints, growth/life-history access to large adults, and ecological opportunity. GigaCascade makes this testable by requiring uncertainty propagation, temporal ordering, negative controls, and held-out lineage prediction. A failure would still be informative by identifying whether current evidence favors simpler environmental, anatomical, or sampling explanations instead.
known_scientific_risks: Fossil incompleteness and taxonomic sampling can confound trait correlations.
Pneumaticity is an anatomical proxy and does not directly observe respiratory or thermal performance.
Growth histology and mass reconstructions retain ontogenetic and method uncertainty.
Comparative causal models can support only conditional historical inferences, not direct experimental proof.
